legislation.notes: PL 2026 c.644, approved 6 April 2026, enacts 35-A MRSA 3475. An 'eligible system' is a plug-in photovoltaic or plug-in battery system with an EXPORT CAPACITY of 1,200 watts or less, listed or certified to UL 3700 or a comparable standard, using inverters configured to shut off within 0.2 seconds if power is disrupted. Subsection 3 sets the tiers in COMBINED INVERTER OUTPUT measured in alternating current: up to 420 W per service address with no further condition; above 420 W and up to 1,200 W each system must be installed by an electrician licensed in the State and use a dedicated circuit with a single outlet. Subsection 5: the customer must notify the utility on a form prescribed by the Commission within 30 days of installation; the utility may not deny a compliant installation. Subsection 4: an eligible system MAY NOT be used for net energy billing under 3209-A or 3209-B. Subsection 8: a customer installing on a structure they do not own must not compromise its integrity or violate state or local building, fire or zoning codes.

watt_tiers.basis: export capacity (definition) / combined inverter output in AC (capacity limits)
watt_tiers.effect: Above 420 W: must be installed by an electrician licensed in Maine, on a dedicated circuit with a single outlet, with notification to the utility within 30 days of installation. No interconnection application, agreement, study, fee or extra equipment. Not eligible for net energy billing.

watt_tiers.basis: combined inverter output, measured in alternating current
watt_tiers.effect: May be installed and operated by the customer with no electrician requirement, no dedicated-circuit requirement and no notification.

legislation.notes: Chapter 262. RSA 362-A:1-a, IV-a defines a 'plug-in solar generation system' as a movable photovoltaic system intended to EXCLUSIVELY offset a portion of onsite consumption, connected through a receptacle or other non-permanent wiring connection. RSA 362-A:10, IV: one system per metered customer with a MAXIMUM INVERTER OUTPUT of 1,200 watts AC. The utility may not require approval, an interconnection review or agreement, a fee, or extra equipment - but 362-A:10, II lets it develop a method for the customer to report the system's wattage AFTER installation, for notification purposes only. 362-A:10, V requires the Department of Energy to publish notice that connecting an unlisted system, or one installed contrary to the state building code or manufacturer instructions, MAY AFFECT HOMEOWNERS OR RENTERS INSURANCE COVERAGE. No HOA, covenant, condominium, landlord or tenant provision appears anywhere in the act.

effective_delayed.summary: The building code review board must amend the state building code to address buildings using a plug-in system. Takes effect only when the commissioner of the Department of Energy certifies to the Office of Legislative Services and the Secretary of State that a nationally recognized standard exists authorising plug-in solar systems to be safely connected to a building's electrical system. No deadline is set.

watt_tiers.effect: One system per metered customer. Exempt from interconnection requirements and agreements and from net energy metering under RSA 362-A:9. No utility approval, review, fee or additional utility-specified equipment.

legislation.cert_required: National Electrical Code + Underwriters Laboratories or equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory
legislation.notes: Introduced 24 February 2026 by Councilmember Allen with Frumin, Lewis George, Nadeau, Parker, Pinto and R. White. Referred to the Committee on Transportation and the Environment 3 March 2026; public hearing 26 March 2026. Adds a new subsection defining a portable solar generation device and exempting it from interconnection and net-metering requirements unless the owner opts in; the Electric Company may not require approval, a fee, or extra controls, and is not liable. The device must meet the most recent National Electrical Code, be certified by UL or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory, and include an anti-islanding feature. As introduced the bill sets no power cap - no wattage limit appears in the provision. Status: Under Council Review, no vote recorded. Verified against lims.dccouncil.gov on 19 August 2026.
